Costume recognisability — Noam's "red cotton snap-front western shirt with short sleeves" and Lio's "green cotton long-sleeve western shirt with a pointed yoke and snap buttons" are western shirts. Noam's "blue bandana" and "brown felt cowboy hat", Lio's "black leather vest", "dark grey denim chaps-style jeans", "tan felt cowboy hat" and "black leather cowboy boots" all belong to the cowboy costume. No garment breaks this check. NONE.
2. Drawability — No garment is described by its knotting, fastening or trim alone. NONE.
3. Colour distinction — The dominant colour of the largest garment is: Noam top red, bottom blue; Lio top green, bottom dark grey (grey); Anna top yellow, bottom blue; Elena top orange, bottom black; Sara top red, bottom brown; Saba top purple, bottom beige; Noe top blue, bottom dark khaki (brown). Two characters share a dominant colour: Noam (top red) and Sara (top red). Both have red as the dominant colour of their largest top garment. Also, Noam's "blue bandana tied around the neck" uses blue, and Anna's bottom is blue — but bandana is not the largest garment. The red top conflict between Noam and Sara is the primary issue. REWRITE ONE.
4. Slot conflicts — Noam wears a bandana tied around the neck (accessories) and a shirt; a bandana and a shirt are compatible. Lio wears a vest over a shirt; both are separate slots. No character wears two garments in the same slot. NONE.
5. Face — The hats have "a gently curled brim pushed back off the eyes". The brim is pushed back, not low, so it does not shadow the eyes. No masks, visors, veils, helmets or crowns. NONE.
6. Completeness — Every character has a top, a bottom and footwear. No character has a tail, fin or fused lower body. No nightwear required by this check alone. NONE.
7. Style world — No world named below. NONE.
8. Sex — Noam (male) wears a snap-front western shirt, jeans, cowboy boots and hat — all boys'/men's forms. Lio (male) wears a western shirt, vest, chaps-style jeans and boots — all boys'/men's forms. Anna, Elena, Sara, Saba (female) wear women's garments. Noe (male) wears men's garments. No garment breaks this check. NONE.
9. Coverage — The locked page plan places the story in a cowboy-themed world. Noam and Lio are the child main characters who are the theme about, and they already have `costumed` entries with `costume: cowboy`. No page puts any character in bed or into pyjamas for a bedtime routine. Anna appears on multiple pages, but no page transforms her into something else. The magpie is an animal; no wardrobe needed. No other character needs a costumed or nightwear entry. NONE.
10. Child coverage — Noam (age 2) and Lio (age 4) are children. Noam's costumed outfit has a short-sleeve shirt covering his torso. Lio's costumed outfit has a long-sleeve shirt covering his torso. Neither has swimwear. No nightwear entries exist. NONE.
11. Garment variety — No two characters wear the same set of garments recoloured. Noam wears a short-sleeve snap-front western shirt, bandana, jeans, cowboy hat, cowboy boots. Lio wears a long-sleeve western shirt with pointed yoke, leather vest, chaps-style jeans, cowboy hat, cowboy boots. Different garment types and silhouettes. NONE.
12. Plot garments — The page plan uses a tin star as a plot object. Page 1: Noe pins a tin star onto Lio's chest, Noam's star already on. Page 13: Lio releases his star onto the post for the magpie. Both Noam and Lio's costumed outfits name "a shiny silver tin sheriff star worn pinned on the shirt chest". This is the same garment type but each boy has his own star — Noam's is already on, Lio's is pinned on him. The plan hands Lio's star to the magpie; Noam's star remains. The plan does not hand Noam's star to anyone else. However, two outfits both name the same garment: a tin sheriff star. The star belongs to the character who wears it first. Noam wears his first (already on in Page 1). Lio receives his from Noe in Page 1. The plan hands Lio's star to the magpie in Page 13. The outfit that should name the star is Lio's, as the plan first gives it to Lio (Noe pins it on him). Noam's star appears already on him; Noam's outfit should also name his own star. But the check says "A garment belongs to ONE outfit: that of the character who wears it first. ... No two outfits name the same garment." Wait — they are two separate physical stars. The check says "Name any garment two outfits both name, and rewrite the outfit of the character who does not wear it first without it." The garment named is "a shiny silver tin sheriff star". Both outfits name it. Noam wears his first (already on). Lio's star is pinned on him later. Lio is the one who does not wear it first; his outfit should not name it, because the star is Noam's garment first? No — each boy has his own star. The plan gives two separate stars. The check is about the same garment being named in two outfits. Since they are identical in wording, it triggers the check. Noam wears his first, so Noam's outfit keeps the star. Lio's star is a different physical star but identical in description; the check flags it. However, the star is absolutely essential to the plot for both boys. The fix: keep the star in Noam's outfit, remove from Lio's — but Lio must wear a star in the story. This creates a plot problem. Actually, the check says "The plan hands Lio's star to the magpie ... the receiver's outfit never names it." Lio's star is handed off. So Lio's outfit should not name the star; the star is a prop given to him on Page 1? No — it's pinned on him as a garment. The star is a garment he wears. The rule is: the first character to wear that garment has it in their outfit. Noam wears his first. Lio's star is a separate instance but described the same. To satisfy the check, remove the star from Lio's outfit and treat his star as a prop given on Page 1. But the check also says: "No two outfits name the same garment." The star is named in both Noam and Lio's outfits. I must remove it from one. Since Noam wears his first, keep Noam's. Remove from Lio. But Lio needs the star for the plot — it will be handled as a prop in the page plan. The outfit rewrite removes it. FAULT: Noam and Lio both name a tin star. REWRITE Lio's outfit without the star.
13. Appearance only — Outfits describe appearance only. No outfit includes page numbers, events, other characters, carried items or pocket contents. NONE.
14. Props — No outfit lists a blanket, towel, sheet, tablecloth, bag, umbrella, toy, tool or other carried object. The star is a garment, not a prop. The bucket, rattle, lead rope, apple, oats are props handled in the plan, not in outfits. NONE.

Additional issues found: Check 3 requires fixing the red top shared by Noam and Sara. Noam's costumed top is red; Sara's standard top is red. Costume recognisability outranks colour distinction for costumed characters, but the fix should not break the costume. Noam's cowboy shirt colour can change to another colour not used as a dominant colour by any other character. Options: Noam's top could become blue — but his jeans are blue, and Anna's jeans are blue, and Noe's jacket is blue. Yellow? Anna's cardigan is yellow. Green? Lio's shirt is green. Orange? Elena's vest is orange. Purple? Saba's sweatshirt is purple. Brown? No one has a brown top. Black? Lio's vest is black, Elena's leggings are black. White? Elena's henley is cream (white). Grey? Lio's chaps are dark grey. The safest change: make Noam's shirt brown, or change Sara's sweater. Since Noam is a costumed character, changing his shirt colour to a cowboy-authentic colour that isn't red works. Brown is a good cowboy colour and no one else has a brown top (Sara's skirt is brown, not her top). Change Noam's shirt to brown. Or change Sara's sweater to another colour — her sweater could be green, but Lio's shirt is green; orange — Elena's vest is orange; purple — Saba's is purple; yellow — Anna's is yellow; white — Elena's henley is cream; grey — no one has a grey top; black — no one has a black top. I'll change Sara's sweater to grey to keep Noam's classic red cowboy shirt, as changing Noam's shirt colour might weaken the costume recognisability (red western shirt is iconic). Wait — the instruction says: "Fixing check 1 outranks fixing check 3: a character in the right costume sharing a colour with someone else is better than a distinct colour on a garment that does not read as the costume." So for a costumed character like Noam, keep the red shirt. Change Sara's standard top instead. Change Sara's sweater to grey. Grey is unclaimed as a top colour (Noe's shirt is grey under his jacket, but his jacket is blue — the largest garment on Noe is the blue jacket; his shirt is an underlayer). Check 3 says "largest garment shares a dominant colour". For Sara, the sweater is her largest top garment. For Noe, the jacket is his largest garment, which is blue. Grey is clear. FAULT: Sara and Noam share red as dominant top colour. REWRITE Sara's top to grey.

Check 12: Lio's star removed. REWRITE Lio's outfit without the star.
